name: Life Insurance Corporation of India
title: Life Insurance Corporation of India - 543526 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: LIC H1 FY27 net VNB rose 33.95% to ₹6,846 crore, with VNB margin up 470 bps to 22.3%, while total APE grew only 5.72% to ₹30,696 crore.
summary.overview: LIC reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) with profit after tax up 21.52% to ₹25,568 crore and net VNB up 33.95% to ₹6,846 crore. Margin expansion came from business mix (non-par savings and term) and assumption changes, partly offset by a 1.4% expense realignment. Individual APE was flat-to-weak because ULIP sales fell sharply, reflecting a deliberate push for higher ticket sizes, while individual NBP grew 14.86%. Solvency improved to 2.35x from 2.13x, but IEV fell 1.95% year on year because of MTM losses on debt.

financial_highlights.change: +470 bps YoY (from 17.6%); Q1 FY27 22.9%, so down ~60 bps QoQ
vs 59.41% a year ago; individual 37.51% (vs 37.21%), group 70.45% (vs 72.74%)

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual APE ₹17,224 crore (56.11% of APE); ULIP APE fell more than 40% as agents shifted to higher-ticket monthly eNACH policies. Non-PAR share of individual APE rose to 34.02% from 36.31%, and PAR was 65.98%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group APE ₹13,472 crore (43.89% of APE), up about 14% per management; group new business premium up 20.63%. Market share fell to 70.45% from 72.74%, which management attributed to the cyclical term-group segment.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: New business premium ₹2,458 crore, up 21.44% YoY; bank channel ₹1,336 crore (+5.56%) and alternate channel ₹1,122 crore (+48.01%). Share of individual NBP rose to 7.53% from 7.12%.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Agency sold 98.4% of policies and 91.81% of new business premium; agent count fell to 14,52,461 from 14,85,325 and agent market share fell to 43.70% from 45.86%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects individual APE growth to converge with individual rated NBP (WRP) growth by year-end, helped by H2 ULIP ticket-size recovery and newly launched health, cancer cover, deferred annuity and term products.
Management says it has a 'very positive outlook on margin for 2027-28', relying on product mix (non-par savings and protection) and expense optimisation, not on RFR benefit.
Q3 and Q4 are historically LIC's strongest quarters for first-year premium and WRP, per management.
Management is still assessing the RBC regime and the IRDAI distribution consultation paper; capital deployment decision deferred until reforms are rolled out.
Management says LIC's expense ratio is comfortably within the proposed distribution-cost caps.
capex_capacity: Office rationalisation is a work in progress, with digital adoption and process re-engineering to roll out over the next few quarters, expected to optimise expenses.
Bima Sakhi network: 3.04 lakh Bima Sakhis, 10.64 lakh policies sold, ₹1,548.80 crore NBP; covers 1,60,928 of 2,44,524 gram panchayats (66%).
Product count: 63 products as of 13 November 2026 (excluding PMJJBY), including 41 exclusive individual products, 13 exclusive group products, seven individual riders and one group rider.
Five new non-par individual products launched in H1; three more launched on 19 October 2026 (Jeevan Dhara-II deferred annuity, Health Shield and New Cancer Cover).
Hedging: about 80% of non-par premium is hedged, with maturities hedged up to 8 years.
demand_pricing: ULIP APE fell more than 40% YoY due to deliberate ticket-size push; monthly eNACH share of ULIP fell from about 24% a year ago to 14%. Protection APE is growing more than 50%.
Persistency (premium basis) at 13M/25M/37M/49M/61M was 74.69%/69.62%/67.17%/64.31%/61.03%, down from 75.29%/71.37%/67.70%/63.70%/63.81%. On a policy-count basis it improved at 13M, 37M and 49M.
Maturity claims ₹1,25,806 crore (+16.93% YoY); death claims ₹12,691 crore (+5.33%).
ANANDA agent-assisted app: 12,40,676 policies completed (+41.23% YoY).
WRP is about 55% of first-year premium and is growing 14.5%-15%, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IRDAI distribution reform (lower commissions) make LIC's agency-led non-par annuity products less competitive versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LIC is comfortable with the proposed expense caps and is well placed given its low overall expense ratio. It expects competitors to need significant work to reach these levels, so it does not foresee a near-term competitive disadvantage.

qa_highlights.question: With solvency at 235%, above a typical 170-190% comfort range, how will capital be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is keeping the current solvency margin under review until RBC and IFRS outcomes are clear, and will decide on profit distribution or capital deployment after the reforms are rolled out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did VNB margin fall from Q1 to Q2 despite better mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said business mix added 0.5% QoQ and the impact of assumptions was -1.2%, driven by an approximately 40 bps fall in RFR. Margin moved from 22.9% in Q1 to 22.3% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual APE growth lagging individual rated NBP growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to a 40%+ fall in ULIP APE caused by the ticket-size push. Savings and protection growth was not enough to offset it, and convergence is expected by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Will LIC keep growing individual APE for FY27 and what about the IDBI Bank stake sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong H2 APE growth from new health and deferred annuity products, term policies (over 100,000 collected), and the 70th-anniversary closed product ending 31 March. On banca, it said IDBI now accounts for about 20% of total bancassurance, and it does not foresee much depletion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY28 without RFR tailwinds, and how do group sub-segments differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to mix (non-par savings, term), expense optimisation and higher-margin group annuity and GTIS growth relative to fund-based group business. It expects a positive margin outlook for 2027-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 individual persistency on a premium basis fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said policy-count persistency improved at 13M/37M/49M, but premium persistency did not improve because persistent policies skew to lower sum-assured and premium cohorts. It called the issue product-agnostic.

risks_watch: Embedded value declined 1.95% YoY to ₹7,97,378 crore; management attributed the negative to MTM losses on debt, while core business was positive.
RFR decline (about 40 bps QoQ) may keep compressing VNB margin, and management says RFR is outside its control.
Agent network shrank (agents down about 2.2% YoY, agent market share 43.70% vs 45.86%) amid possible commission cuts under the IRDAI consultation paper.
ULIP recovery depends on market conditions; ULIP APE is down more than 40%.
Group market share fell about 230 bps YoY to 70.45%; group APE growth is cyclical and dependent on large term-group tenders.
Persistency on premium basis weakened in several cohorts (13M, 25M, 37M, 61M).
Bancassurance growth depends on IDBI Bank (about 20% of total banca) and on the bank partner mix after the IDBI privatisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and VNB, but cautious and at times evasive on growth in individual APE, persistency, and the distribution-reform outcome, with management repeatedly deferring to H2 recovery and final regulator decisions. Several answers were vague or went off-topic (for example, the VNB breakup requested by analysts was not provided).
key_quotes: We expect the margins to improve further, and we will be going closer to the other players in the listed space.
We have a very positive outlook on margin for 2027-28 as well.
So we are very confident that we will be able to show a very healthy growth as far as the APE is concerned.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management expects individual APE growth to converge with WRP growth (~14.5-15%) by year-end, backed only by H2 ULIP ticket-size recovery and newly launched products, with no capacity or order specifics, and expects a positive margin outlook for FY28 without numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VNB margin was 22.3% in H1 (up 470 bps YoY from 17.6%) on non-par savings and term mix plus a 1.4% expense realignment; management has a 'very positive outlook on margin for 2027-28' without relying on RFR, though Q2 margin already slipped ~60 bps QoQ from 22.9% on a ~40 bps RFR fall.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches are discussed; the only related item is office rationalisation to cut expenses, and the agent count fell to 14,52,461 from 14,85,325.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4 seasonally strongest)
rows.why: Total APE grew only 5.72% to ₹30,696 crore and individual APE is lagging, with ULIP APE down more than 40%; management expects convergence with WRP growth of ~14.5-15% by year-end, but this depends on the ULIP ticket-size recovery.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Solvency rose to 2.35x from 2.13x and management is deferring capital deployment until RBC and distribution reforms are clear, which points away from a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance was given; management's outlook is qualitative and it is cautious on individual APE, persistency and the distribution-reform outcome.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Premium persistency fell at 25M (69.62% vs 71.37%), 37M (67.17% vs 67.70%) and 61M (61.03% vs 63.81%), and IRDAI commission caps and RFR declines could compress margins.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Five non-par products launched in H1 and three more on 19 October 2026 (Jeevan Dhara-II, Health Shield, New Cancer Cover), with management expecting H2 APE growth from the new health and deferred annuity products.

rows.label: IRDAI distribution reform and commission caps
rows.why: Management says its expense ratio (10.41%, down 87 bps YoY) is within the proposed caps and it sees no near-term disadvantage, but agent count fell about 2.2% and the outcome is still pending.

rows.label: Capital deployment decision on 2.35x solvency
rows.why: Solvency of 2.35x is above the 170-190% comfort range cited on the call, but management will decide on distribution or deployment only after the reforms roll out.

rows.label: Bima Sakhi and alternate-channel growth
rows.why: Alternate channel NBP rose 48.01% to ₹1,122 crore and Bima Sakhi covers 66% of gram panchayats with ₹1,548.80 crore NBP, supporting volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on VNB margin and the FY28 margin outlook, but cautious and deferring on individual APE, persistency and the distribution-reform outcome; analysts pushed on the ULIP-driven APE lag and the falling Q2 margin versus Q1.
